body.title: Wire the sequencer behind registerBuildRunners, emit outcome progress, and persist the outcome list incrementally
body.summary: Drive the sequencer from the build stage's start/decompose/synthesize/finalize turn handlers registered via registerBuildRunners() (sc1, owned by s1) — adding the sequencing turn behind the existing registration without re-registering or mutating sibling stages. Emit BuildTaskOutcome progress at every Task boundary (task-start, implementer-finished, test-verdict, advance-or-halt) through the WorkflowStepOutputBuild / WorkflowProgress driving surface (sc2, owned by s1), keeping a single source of truth for Task status — no second store. Own the durability NFR explicitly: supply the storage-writer implementation behind the sequencer's per-Task-boundary checkpoint hook (t6) so the accumulated BuildTaskOutcome[] is persisted through the existing hash-json/storage writers AT EACH Task boundary, not only at finalize — because build (unlike define/design/plan) mutates the working tree non-transactionally, a daemon restart mid-run must leave a readable record of what already landed. All stage-boundary logging goes through getLogger('workflow:build'), never console.log (migration step 7; interactionWithShared sc1/sc2; observability + durability NFR).
acceptanceChecks: The sequencer runs behind the build stage handlers registered by registerBuildRunners(); no sibling stage (define / design.epic / design.story / tracker) is re-registered or mutated, and BuildTaskOutcome data is emitted at each Task boundary through the WorkflowStepOutputBuild / WorkflowProgress surface with no second source of truth for Task status.

The accumulated BuildTaskOutcome[] is persisted incrementally at each Task boundary via the sequencer's checkpoint hook through the existing hash-json/storage writers (not only at finalize), so a simulated mid-run restart leaves a readable record of the outcomes already landed; halts name the failed Task + reason + blocked set, and all logging uses getLogger('workflow:build').

tests.name: wiring: the sequencing turn runs behind registerBuildRunners() without re-registering sibling stages, emits BuildTaskOutcome at each Task boundary through the WorkflowStepOutputBuild/WorkflowProgress surface, and the checkpoint hook persists the accumulated outcomes at each boundary so a simulated mid-run restart leaves a readable record
